author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: The Dashwood family had lived comfortably at Norland Park in Sussex for a long time.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: The old owner of the estate invited his nephew Henry Dashwood to live there, and they were happy.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: When the old man died, he left the estate to Henry's son from his first marriage, leaving Henry's current family without the money.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: The old man liked Henry's grandson, Harry, so much that he left him the estate instead of the nieces who cared for him.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Henry Dashwood was disappointed but hoped to save money while he lived.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Henry Dashwood died only a year later, leaving his family with very little money.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Before dying, Henry asked his son John to help take care of his stepmother and half-sisters.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: John promised to help, though he was a selfish man who only cared about money.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: John's wife was even more selfish than he was.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: After the funeral, John considered giving his sisters a thousand pounds each.
